Spectral Geometry and Topological Data Analysis
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Spectral-Geometric Correspondence: Deriving global geometric invariants, such as leaf space volumes, by analyzing the asymptotic growth of the basic spectrum via Weyl’s Law and Hilbert series expansions.

Equivariant Convexification: Reducing complex non-convex optimization problems over orbit spaces into tractable semidefinite programming formulations by characterizing invariant spectrahedra through equivariant linear matrix inequalities.

Metric-Topological Synthesis: Establishing rigid geometric constraints and classification theorems for submanifolds by linking extrinsic diameter bounds and focal radius characterizations to the algebraic structure of polar representations and singular Riemannian foliations.

Algebraic-Geometric Duality: Utilizing inverse invariant theory and separating sets to reconstruct the topology of orbit spaces and tangent cones from the algebraic properties of polynomial invariants and real zero polynomials.
Summary Description: Ricardo Mendes specializes in the intersection of Representation Theory, Invariant Theory, and Riemannian Geometry, with significant contributions to Spectral Geometry and Convex Algebraic Geometry. His research bridges abstract algebraic structures with metric geometry, focusing on orbit spaces of compact group representations and singular Riemannian foliations. Key achievements include proving the maximality of Laplacian algebras, establishing equivariant descriptions of invariant spectrahedra, and deriving Weyl’s Law for singular foliations. By linking spectral asymptotics to Hilbert series, Mendes enables precise volume computations and rationality results for leaf spaces. His work provides powerful tools for symmetry-reduced optimization and the classification of submanifolds, demonstrating a profound synthesis of spectral analysis, enumerative combinatorics, and geometric topology.
